summary: 61 exploratory drags over 12 positions (g04 x3, g05 x4, g07 x2, g09 x1, g10 x2). (a) Playing the move that was actually played in the game (8 cases) simply steps onto that main-line ply: the review's own display (coach green/red/orange arrows and 0.8 overlays) appears at 0 ms. (b) Playing the review's precomputed best move for that position when it differs from the game move (3 cases: g6# at g05.p059 graded in ~21 ms, Qe2 at g05.p012 and Qxf5 at g09.p044 at 0 ms) is graded Best at once and shows NO arrow. (b2) Re-playing an already explored move (1 case) re-uses its node, grade and blue arrow at 0 ms. (c) Every other move (49 cases) is graded 1508-1536 ms after the drop (median ~1522 ms; pick-up to drop ~250 ms) and then shows exactly ONE arrow: BLUE rgba(72,193,249,0.8) at opacity 0.8, the engine's best move for the side now to move (a capture, the mating move, a quiet move - whatever is best), drawn with the same geometry as review arrows. No green, red or orange arrows and no 0.8 overlays ever appear on explored moves, whatever their grade (blunder, miss, excellent, best). The arrow appears once and does not update. (d) A second explored ply in the same variation behaves the same (blue arrow for the next side). (e) ArrowLeft inside a variation restores that ply's blue arrow; leaving the variation restores the main-line display; ArrowRight from the branch point follows the main line. Re-playing an already explored move re-uses its node and shows grade + arrow at 0 ms.
